newsitem.title: USA: UPS, Teamsters talks recess until noon Friday.
newsitem.headline: UPS, Teamsters talks recess until noon Friday.

text.p: United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union ended contract talks just after midnight on Thursday and agreed to continue negotiating at noon on Friday in a bid to end the strike crippling the nation's largest parcel carrier.
"After 10 and a half hours of talks, the parties agreed to break off talks and recess until noon," federal mediator John Calhoun Wells told reporters after UPS officials left the talks.

Teamsters President Ron Carey told reporters as he emerged from the talks -- which began around 2:30 p.m. EDT on Thursday -- that neither side had made any concessions but they agreed to come back to the bargaining table later on Friday.
"We're talking about all the major problems," Carey said. "We should be trying to meet some common or middle ground."

The union issued a statement late on Thursday saying the two sides had reached an impasse and urging Teamsters around the country to keep up pressure on the company. But after the talks recessed, Carey said he felt the company had gained a better understanding of the issues during the discussions.
"The ball, we think, is in their court," he said, adding his hope that an agreement could be hammered out when talks resumed later on Friday.
